precepts.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. Such as leave it, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.
precepts.point: The truth for us is the only thing we have to get up out of here. This is all we have. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death. And what God is really asking of us is a small thing in comparison to the sins that we have committed. So what is hard about not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath day holy? Those are minor things. Minor, in the scope of eternal life.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

precepts.text: For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time. The she that is inhabited by devils is America. That great time goes into the thousand years; Revelation 20 goes into when hell gives up the dead and everything is destroyed.
precepts.point: Remember the demons that said, Art thou come hither to torment us before the time? That place of torment is going to be set up here after this place is destroyed physically.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us”. Moses understood that we would be brought into spiritual Egypt, America, and he saw America being destroyed. That is what Revelation 18 shows: “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.”

What does hold mean? A hold is like a prison. After America is destroyed, America will become a prison, a cage. The demons that said, art thou come hither to torment us before the time? That torment is going to take place here in America.

Baruch 4:35: “For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.” The she that will be inhabited by devils is America. This place is going to be the place of torment, the prison of those same devils. When America is destroyed and Christ returns, he is going to set up a lake of fire, spiritual damnation, here in America for all the wicked.

“For a great time”: that great time is the thousand years. Revelation 20 goes into it, when hell gives up the dead and everything is destroyed. So Babylon becomes the habitation of devils, burning with a fire from the Everlasting that is long to endure.

precepts.text: This is the book of the commandments of God and the law that endureth forever; all they that keep it shall come to life. O Israel, happy are we, for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.
precepts.point: Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins. What is pleasing to God is his laws.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

precepts.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life, but such as leave it shall die. The churches say the law is done away, yet keep tithing, the one law that is, which proves they are covetous.
precepts.point: There are plenty of books, but this is the book of life. It is the one you have to be reading.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Blessed is he that readeth”. We all want blessings, and here is the formula. Read four chapters a day and you finish the Bible in a year; if you have more time, read more. Reading is how you hear the word, “and they that hear the words of this prophecy”, and hearing is how you apply it, “and keep those things which are written therein”. You read “thou shalt not steal”, you keep it, and nobody will ever call you a thief. That is how the blessing comes.

But what should you be reading? There are plenty of good books, but this is the book of life. Baruch says: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever”. If you want to know which commandments to follow, you read the whole Bible, and the law endures forever.

So the Christian churches are lost in the sauce. They say you don’t have to keep any laws, yet they keep the one law that actually is done away with, tithing. That proves they are greedy dogs and covetous men, and all their lights are going to be put out. Coming out of that church and seeing that covetousness is a bad thing, why would we come into the truth and still be covetous?

“All they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” If you want life, if you don’t want your light put out, you keep the commandments: read the Bible, learn the laws, statutes and commandments, and apply them. You tell me, do you want life or death? Being here shows you want life; the question is whether you will do what it takes, or revert to the old man and give in to your lust.

precepts.text: My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you, for thine enemy hath persecuted thee, but shortly thou shalt see his destruction and tread upon his neck.
precepts.point: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. By that measure eighty years is under two hours to God. That is why God calls our trials a small moment.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Peter says “that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” David says our days are seventy, eighty years. Do the math: if a thousand years is one day to God, eighty years is 0.08 of a day, about an hour and fifty-five minutes. An entire human lifetime is less than two hours to God, and it may be even less than that; the concept of time does not apply to the Ancient of days. Eighty years and you come back and God says, you just left, why you back already?

That is why the scriptures say things like Baruch: “My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee”. It is happening right now. We are going through it, and it seems like forever, because down here it takes forever to become an adult, to get your license, to turn 21. Lord, come save us; they are doing their worst.

Then, “but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” Shortly: in less than a few minutes of God's time your life is over, and in an hour or so you see the destruction of your enemy and have a lifetime of God time, eternal. So suffer patiently. What seems long to us is short to him.

precepts.text: Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof.
precepts.point: Ye are the light of the world; a city set on a hill cannot be hid. Keeping the commandments makes Israel stand out, and when they ask where you are from, don't hide it.

note.label: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.why:
Where does the light of Matthew 5 come from? Baruch says: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” That is the end if you reject it.

“Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: take hold of the book of the commandments. “Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: the light is the commandments in the book. Walk in them, “that thou mayest be illuminated.” Enlightened. You become a light in a dark place, the light that cannot be hid.

That is why “A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” Come to this truth and start applying the laws of God and the commandments, and you cannot hide. You dress different, act different, walk different, talk different. How was your Christmas? I don't celebrate that. How was your New Year? I took a nap; a regular day. Thanksgiving, birthdays, the same. And they keep prying: where you from? Who learned you? Esau asks it, Ishmael asks it, Moab asks it, because they see something different in you, that spark, that light.

So don't hide it. “Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel”; you came to this truth to bring forth the wisdom and the light, giving light to the house of our people Israel. “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works”, so our people may see it and maybe take that light themselves and repent.

precepts.text: The law endures for ever: all that keep it come to life, and such as leave it shall die.
precepts.point: There is no breath and no life in Islam, none in Christianity, none in any man-made religion.

note.label: Ezekiel 37:1-11 | Excerpt from “The 4 Temples of Jerusalem”

precepts.text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead. There is a reason why, when you look at those old photos, you look run down, tired. You are twenty-one years old looking forty. This is supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. And we wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday. That is what the Lord said: you break my commandments and you are going to be groping, walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something. All confused in the spirit. Even though the sun is at the apex, you cannot see. We were blinded. We were distracted.
precepts.point: All they that keep it shall come to life. That is just like us. Do you ever look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world? You look dead. You look spiritually dead. That is why the Bible says the law is a spirit. The commandments are spirit.

note.label: Ignite Your Influence

precepts.why:
Baruch says the law “endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Since the beginning of time this law has been in place. Break it and judgments come upon you; keep it and blessings come upon you. Solomon shows what happens to those who leave it: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

Look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world. You look dead, spiritually dead. Run down and tired, twenty-one years old looking forty, when that was supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. We wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. That is why the law is called a spirit: the commandments are spirit, and without them there is no life in us.

They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday, what the Lord said would come on us for breaking his commandments: walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something, all confused in the spirit. Even with the sun at its apex we could not see. We were blinded. We were distracted.

So the law is the difference between the living and the dead. Those who keep it come to life, the way we did when we came into this truth; those who wander from it remain in the congregation of the dead.

precepts.text: The word of God is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endureth for ever; the name, the word, and the law go hand in hand.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

note.label: Deuteronomy 5: The Ten Commandments Reiterated

precepts.why:
“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” The word of God is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endureth for ever.

His name is called The Word of God, and the word is the book of the commandments: the name, the word and the law go hand in hand. So to take the name of the Lord thy God in vain is to break the commandments, as Solomon shows, “lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” They that keep the law shall come to life, and such as leave it shall die, for “the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.”

precepts.text: This is the book of the Commandments; the whole book is the law, so there is no single list. Those that keep it come to life, but such as leave it shall die.
precepts.point: Prayer is largely invalid if there is no action behind it. If you ask for a home but take no steps toward the finances, why would you receive it. Faith without works is dead.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
“O Lord my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.” We will sing thanks to the Most High for ever in the kingdom, but only if we do what we are supposed to do. Baruch shows what that is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

The whole book is the law, so there is no single list to check off. Those that keep it come to life, the life David looks to when he asks whether the dust can praise the Most High or declare his truth; such as leave it shall die. Keeping the book is the action behind the prayer, and without that action the prayer is largely invalid.

precepts.text: When our mind goes astray and we end up in sin, we return and seek him ten times more; committing iniquity does not mean you cannot recover strength.
precepts.point: Everybody who comes into the truth is going to mess up and commit transgression, and everybody ends up where David ended up, having to ask forgiveness and be pardoned. The Lord continually afflicted David for his iniquity, and a lot of us are being afflicted for our iniquities to this very day, so we must come to the Lord with this mindset.

note.label: Psalm 39: David Mourns His Frailty and Prays to Recover Strength

precepts.why:
“O spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go hence, and be no more.” Spare me that I may recover strength means forgive my sins so I may bounce back before I die. Baruch shows how the bouncing back is done: “For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more.” When our mind goes astray and we end up in sin, we return and seek him ten times more. Committing iniquity does not mean you cannot recover strength.

That should be our thought too. Nobody knows when they will die; you could die tomorrow or in two seconds from a bullet, so your main focus must be to recover your strength before you go to the grave.

Everybody who comes into the truth is going to mess up and commit transgression, and everybody ends up where David ended up, having to ask forgiveness and be pardoned. The Lord continually afflicted David for his iniquity, and a lot of us are being afflicted for our iniquities to this very day, so we must come to the Lord with this mindset: “Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear unto my cry; hold not thy peace at my tears”.

precepts.text: The law endures for ever, and Jacob is told to walk in the presence of the light of the commandments that he may be illuminated; the Israelites are the ones to be illuminated to shine upon this earth.
precepts.point: Make Thy face to shine upon Thy servant, and teach me Thy statutes. A man's wisdom makes his face to shine, so the Israelites are to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness. Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not Thy law.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated.”

The law endures for ever, and Jacob is told to take hold of it and walk in the presence of its light that he may be illuminated. The Israelites are the ones to be illuminated with the wisdom of the law, to shine upon this earth: letting our light shine among all nations in this kingdom of darkness.

That is the face made to shine, and the entrance of his words that giveth light and understanding unto the simple, the same as verse 105, where the word is the lamp and the light.

precepts.text: Those who afflicted and rejoiced over Israel will be grieved for their own desolation, and fire shall come upon Babylon the great.
precepts.point: Even in judgment our forefathers still prayed for the destruction of the enemy, asking the Most High to render to them all their wickedness and do to them as He had done to Jerusalem.

note.label: Lamentations 1: The City That Sits Solitary

precepts.why:
Even in judgment our forefathers still prayed for the destruction of the enemy: “Let all their wickedness come before thee; and do unto them, as thou hast done unto me for all my transgressions.” Baruch gives the answer to that prayer. “Miserable are they that afflicted thee, and rejoiced at thy fall. Miserable are the cities which thy children served: miserable is she that received thy sons.”

Her enemies “are glad that thou hast done it”; but “as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation. For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning.”

“For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.” Those who afflicted and rejoiced over Israel will be grieved for their own desolation, and fire shall come upon Babylon the great. The day the Most High has called will come, and “they shall be like unto me.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: The book of Baruch, in the Apocrypha; it's not canon? Well, the hell with you too. You don't tell us what books to read and not to read. You ever hear Esau tell you not to read from there because it is not canon? This is our book; these are our records. But he tells you to read that Christopher Columbus discovered America. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life;” You see that: all they that keep it shall come to life. This is what Ezekiel 37:10 is: the breath came into them and they lived; they got the law and sought to keep it. “but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave it shall die. Damn.

Even if you die today or tomorrow, you are going to see it, because the Lord is going to bring you back. This new Passover has a resurrection taking place too: the Lord is not just coming to destroy, he is bringing souls back with him.
